questions.stem: Convert the polar coordinates (5, π/3) to rectangular coordinates (x, y).
questions.explanation:
The conversion formula from polar to rectangular coordinates is (x, y) = (r 
cos(θ), r 
sin(θ)). Make sure to use the correct angle measure.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Using the wrong angle (π instead of π/3). Remember to use the given θ value in the conversion formula.

questions.stem: Convert the polar coordinates (2, 5π/4) to rectangular coordinates (x, y).
questions.explanation:
The conversion formula from polar to rectangular coordinates is (x, y) = (r 
cos(θ), r 
sin(θ)). Make sure to use the correct angle measure.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Forgetting to adjust the sine and cosine values for the fourth quadrant. The angles in the fourth quadrant have negative cosine and sine values.

questions.stem: Convert the polar coordinates (3, -π/2) to rectangular coordinates (x, y).

The conversion formula from polar to rectangular coordinates is (x, y) = (r 
cos(θ), r 
sin(θ)). Make sure to use the correct angle measure.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Not considering the negative sine value for -π/2. The sine of an angle in the third quadrant is negative.

questions.stem: Convert the polar coordinates (4, 3π) to rectangular coordinates (x, y).

(x, y) = (r 
cos(θ), r 
sin(θ)). For (4, 3π): x = 4 
cos(3π) = -4, y = 4 
sin(3π) = 0.
